mainTopic: The special Torah readings and הפטרות for fast days, weekdays, the holidays, חנוכה, פורים and ראש חודש
overview: The משנה finishes its list of special Torah readings. On fast days we read the ברכות וקללות, and one person reads all the curses. On Mondays, Thursdays and שבת מנחה we read the start of the coming פרשה without moving forward. Each holiday gets its own reading, based on the פסוק 'וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳'. The גמרא then quotes a long ברייתא that gives the Torah reading and הפטרה for פסח, שבועות, ראש השנה, יום הכפורים, סוכות and שמיני עצרת. Along the way it adds how we read 'nowadays', when חוץ לארץ keeps two days of יום טוב. Prompted by the יום כפור הפטרה, רבי יוחנן teaches that wherever תנ״ך shows God's might, it also shows His humility, with a proof from תורה, נביאים and כתובים. The amud ends with רב הונא's rule for שבת חול המועד, the readings for חנוכה, פורים and ראש חודש, and the start of a new statement by רב הונא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blessings and curses are read without a break
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that on fast days the ברכות וקללות are read, and one person reads all the קללות without interruption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blessings and curses. We do not interrupt in the curses. Rather, one person reads all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of special readings: on fast days we read the ברכות וקללות. It adds that the curses must not be split between two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ברכות וקללות' is the end of a list that began on the previous amud. That list ties each special day to its reading, and here the day is תעניות (fast days). The new rule is about how the curses are read: normally a reading is divided among several עולים, but the קללות are kept as one unit read by one person.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings and curses section (ויקרא כ״ו, בחוקותי)
We do not interrupt or break off
One person reads all of them

phrases.english: Blessings and curses.
phrases.notes: The end of the list: on fast days, this is the reading.

phrases.english: We do not interrupt in the curses,
phrases.notes: We do not stop partway and call up a new person.

phrases.english: rather, one person reads all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of special readings on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days the ברכות וקללות are read, and the curses are read straight through by one reader.

steps.title: Weekday and שבת afternoon readings
steps.stepSummary: On Monday, Thursday and שבת מנחה we read from the next פרשה, but these readings do not move the place forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday, Thursday, and on שבת at מנחה, we read in their order, and these do not count toward the reckoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule for the small readings during the week. We read the start of the upcoming פרשה, but we do not advance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קורין כסדרן' means we begin the פרשה that comes after the one read last שבת morning. 'אין עולים להם מן החשבון' means these readings do not move us ahead: Monday does not continue where שבת מנחה stopped. Each of them reads the same opening section again, until the full reading on the next שבת morning.

keyTerms.meaning: On Monday and Thursday
The afternoon prayer
In their regular weekly order
They do not count toward advancing the reading

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין עולים מן החשבון' does NOT mean these readings are worthless or don't count as קריאת התורה. It only means they don't move the place forward. The next שבת starts the whole פרשה from the beginning.

phrases.english: On Monday and on Thursday,
on Shabbat at the afternoon service —
we read in their order,
phrases.notes: From the start of the upcoming weekly portion.

phrases.english: and they do not count toward the reckoning.
phrases.notes: The place in the Torah does not move forward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from fast-day readings to the regular weekday and שבת מנחה readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weekday and שבת מנחה readings use the coming פרשה but do not advance the cycle.

steps.title: Verse source for reading about each holiday in its time
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a פסוק showing that each holiday's section should be read at its own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And משה spoke the appointed times of ה׳ to the children of Israel.' Their מצוה is that each one be read in its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a source from the Torah for the rule that on holidays we read the section about that holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says משה 'spoke the מועדים' to the people. The משנה reads this to mean that part of the מצוה of each holiday is reading its own section on that day. This is the basis for all the holiday readings the גמרא will list next.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a verse)
The appointed times (holidays) of ה׳
In its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: Each holiday gets its own Torah reading on that day. This comes from the פסוק 'וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the base for the whole list of יום טוב readings that the גמרא now goes through.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And Moses spoke

phrases.aramaic: אֶת מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
phrases.english: the appointed times of the Lord to the children of Israel,"
their מצוה is that they should read
each and every one in its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural support for the holiday-reading rule in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that each holiday's section is read on that holiday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כ״ג:מ״ד, 'וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳ אל בני ישראל'.

steps.title: פסח reading and הפטרה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on פסח we read פרשת מועדות and the הפטרה is the פסח celebrated at גלגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. The רבנן taught: On פסח we read the portion of the festivals, and the הפטרה is the פסח of גלגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that spells out the exact readings for each holiday, starting with פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gave the general rule of reading about each holiday. The ברייתא gives the details. For פסח, the Torah reading is פרשת מועדות (ויקרא כ״ב–כ״ג), and the הפטרה is the account in יהושע ה׳ of the first פסח in ארץ ישראל, at גלגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
The Torah section listing the festivals
They read as the הפטרה (Prophets reading)
The פסח brought at גלגל in the days of יהושע

phrases.english: Gemara. The Rabbis taught:
On Passover we read from the portion of the festivals
and the haftarah is the Passover of Gilgal,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּפֶסַח קוֹרִין בְּפָרָשַׁת מוֹעֲדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of the משנה's general rule about holiday readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פסח we read פרשת מועדות, and the הפטרה is פסח גלגל.

steps.title: הפטרות for the two days of פסח nowadays
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays, with two days of יום טוב, the first day's הפטרה is פסח גלגל and the second day's is פסח יאשיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when there are two days, on the first day it is the פסח of גלגל, and on the next day it is the פסח of יאשיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds to the ברייתא: since today there are two days of יום טוב, it assigns a separate הפטרה to the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of a single day of יום טוב. Outside ארץ ישראל we keep יום טוב שני, so the second day needs its own הפטרה. The גמרא keeps פסח גלגל for the first day and gives the second day the פסח of יאשיהו המלך (מלכים ב׳ כ״ג).

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays
Two days (of יום טוב)
The פסח celebrated by יאשיהו המלך

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for our practice in חוץ לארץ of having a different הפטרה on the second day of יום טוב.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when there are two days,
on the first day — the Passover of Gilgal,
and on the next day — the Passover of Josiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the ברייתא's ruling for the current situation of two יום טוב days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two days of יום טוב, day one's הפטרה is פסח גלגל and day two's is פסח יאשיהו.

steps.title: The middle days of Passover use a collection of Passover sections
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: on the remaining days of פסח, one gathers and reads various Torah sections that deal with פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on the other days of פסח, one collects and reads from sections that deal with the topic of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on from the first day of פסח to the in-between days (חול המועד). It says there is no single fixed section; we pick from several places that talk about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day there was one clear section (פרשת מועדות). For the other days, the ברייתא says to choose from different Torah sections that share the topic of פסח. It does not say which ones, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The other (remaining) days of Passover
Gathers or collects (picks readings from different places)
From its topic (sections connected to the subject)

phrases.english: And on the other days of Passover
one collects and reads
from the topic of Passover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 4, moving from the first day of פסח to the remaining days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the remaining days of פסח, we read a selection of Torah sections that deal with פסח.

steps.title: Which sections are these?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific sections the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: which Torah sections count as "the topic of פסח"? This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a general guideline without a list. The גמרא is not challenging the rule. It only wants the actual sections identified.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request to identify something)

phrases.english: What are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the general rule in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific Torah sections are read on the middle days of פסח.

steps.title: רב פפא's memory aid: מאפ"ו
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a memory aid, מאפ"ו, in which each letter stands for one of the readings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the memory aid is מ-א-פ-ו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question with a memory device. Each letter is the first letter of a Torah section about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מ stands for "משכו וקחו לכם" (the פסח offering in Egypt). א stands for "אם כסף תלוה" (which includes the שלש רגלים). פ stands for "פסל לך" (which mentions חג המצות). ו stands for "וידבר ה' אל משה במדבר סיני" (פסח שני and the פסח in the desert). These four sections fill the middle days.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory aid (mnemonic)
The initials of the four readings: מְשְׁכוּ, אִם כֶּסֶף, פְּסׇל לְךָ, וַיְדַבֵּר

steps.confusionAlert: מאפ"ו is not a word with a meaning. It is just four first letters put together so you can remember the four readings.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Mem-Alef-Peh-Vav is the mnemonic.
phrases.notes: משכו, אם כסף, פסל לך, וידבר

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The four readings are משכו, אם כסף, פסל לך, and וידבר, remembered as מאפ"ו.

steps.title: Readings for the last day of Passover and the day after
steps.stepSummary: On the last יום טוב of פסח we read ויהי בשלח with the הפטרה of וידבר דוד. On the next day (in חוץ לארץ) we read כל הבכור with the הפטרה of עוד היום.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the last יום טוב of פסח we read "ויהי בשלח" and the הפטרה is "וידבר דוד." On the next day we read "כל הבכור" and the הפטרה is "עוד היום."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the readings for the final day of פסח. It then adds the readings for the extra day kept outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seventh day is when the sea split, so we read the story of קריעת ים סוף and the שירה. The matching הפטרה is דוד's song of thanks. On the eighth day we read כל הבכור, which mentions פסח. The הפטרה עוד היום tells of סנחריב's fall, which happened on the night of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The last holiday day (שביעי של פסח)
The section of קריעת ים סוף and אז ישיר
And they read as the הפטרה
And on the next day (the eighth day, in חוץ לארץ)

phrases.english: On the last festival day of Passover
they read "And it came to pass when Pharaoh sent",
and for the haftara "And David spoke".
And on the next day, "All the firstborn",
and for the haftara "This very day".

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח קוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the middle days to the last day(s) of פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seventh day: ויהי בשלח with the הפטרה וידבר דוד. Eighth day: כל הבכור with the הפטרה עוד היום.

steps.title: אביי reports today's custom for all eight days
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that nowadays everyone reads according to the memory aid: משך תורא, קדש בכספא, פסל במדברא, שלח בוכרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: nowadays everyone is used to reading: "Draw the bull, sanctify with money, hew in the desert, send the firstborn."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells us how people actually read on the eight days of פסח in his time. He uses a memory sentence in which each two-word pair stands for two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משך = משכו, תורא = שור או כשב (the holiday section in ויקרא). קדש = קדש לי כל בכור, כספא = אם כסף. פסל = פסל לך, מדברא = וידבר במדבר סיני. שלח = ויהי בשלח, בוכרא = כל הבכור. This gives a full eight-day order and adds the readings שור או כשב and קדש לי.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone is accustomed (the common custom)
Bull (hint to "שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב")
Firstborn (hint to "כׇּל הַבְּכוֹר")

steps.confusionAlert: Each pair of words covers two different days, so the four pairs cover eight days. It is not one reading per pair.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the order of readings on פסח that is used in חוץ לארץ today.

phrases.english: Abaye said: and nowadays
everyone is accustomed to read:
draw the bull, sanctify with money,
hew in the desert, send the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, וְהָאִידָּנָא נְהוּג עָלְמָא לְמִיקְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Updates the ברייתא's readings with the custom of אביי's time for all eight days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eight days are read in order: משכו, שור או כשב, קדש, אם כסף, פסל, במדבר, ויהי בשלח, כל הבכור.

steps.title: Two opinions about the reading for שבועות
steps.stepSummary: On עצרת the first opinion reads שבעה שבועות with a הפטרה from חבקוק. אחרים say to read בחדש השלישי with the הפטרה of the מרכבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On עצרת we read "שבעה שבועות" and the הפטרה is from חבקוק. Others say: "בחדש השלישי" and the הפטרה is the מרכבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to שבועות and gives two different opinions about what to read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion reads the holiday's own section about counting seven weeks, with a הפטרה from חבקוק that hints at מתן תורה. The אחרים focus on מתן תורה itself: they read the story of הר סיני, with יחזקאל's vision of the מרכבה, since ה' was revealed with a heavenly chariot at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: The name חז"ל use for שבועות
The prophet חבקוק (the הפטרה from chapter 3)
Others say (a second, unnamed opinion)
The heavenly chariot seen by יחזקאל (יחזקאל chapter 1)

phrases.english: On Shavuot, "Seven weeks",
and the haftara is from Habakkuk.
Others say: "In the third month",
and the haftara is the Chariot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from פסח to the next holiday, שבועות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: either שבעה שבועות with חבקוק, or בחדש השלישי with the מרכבה.

steps.title: With two days, we follow both opinions in reverse order
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays, since שבועות has two days, we follow both opinions, but in reverse order: בחדש השלישי on the first day and שבעה שבועות on the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, since there are two days, we do like both opinions, but in reverse order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dispute in practice. With two days of יום טוב, each opinion gets a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Reverse" means the second opinion, the אחרים (בחדש השלישי with the מרכבה), is read on the first day, and the first opinion (שבעה שבועות with חבקוק) is read on the second day. The main day, the day of מתן תורה, gets the reading about מתן תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two days (of יום טוב, in חוץ לארץ)
Like both of them (both opinions)
And in reverse (the opposite order)

steps.whatToRemember: פסח: first day פרשת מועדות, middle days מאפ"ו (or אביי's eight-day order), last days ויהי בשלח and כל הבכור. שבועות: day one בחדש השלישי with the מרכבה, day two שבעה שבועות with חבקוק.
steps.confusionAlert: "Reverse" does not mean we change the readings themselves. It only means the opinion listed second is read on the first day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is exactly the practice followed today on שבועות in חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when there are two days,
we act according to both of them, and in reverse order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles in practice the dispute recorded in Step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On the two days of שבועות we read both opinions: בחדש השלישי on day one and שבעה שבועות on day two.

steps.title: The readings for ראש השנה: two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the ראש השנה reading as בחדש השביעי with the הפטרה of הבן יקיר לי אפרים. יש אומרים reads וה׳ פקד את שרה with the הפטרה about חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה we read 'In the seventh month,' and the הפטרה is 'Is אפרים My dear son?' Some say we read 'And God remembered שרה,' and the הפטרה is the story of חנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to ראש השנה and gives two opinions about what to read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses the section of the Torah that lists the ראש השנה offerings, together with a הפטרה about God remembering His people. The יש אומרים opinion picks stories of שרה and חנה, two women who, according to tradition, were remembered on ראש השנה and given children.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year, the day of judgment
'In the seventh month', the Torah section about the ראש השנה offerings
And some say: a second opinion
Remembered or visited, meaning God remembered שרה and gave her a child
They read as the הפטרה (the reading from the Prophets)

phrases.english: On Rosh HaShana: 'In the seventh month,'
and for the haftara: 'Is Ephraim My dear son?'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ל״א, about God remembering His people

phrases.english: And some say: 'And God remembered Sarah,'
and for the haftara they read about Hannah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's holiday-by-holiday list, moving from עצרת to ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: בחדש השביעי with הבן יקיר. יש אומרים: פקד את שרה with חנה.

steps.title: Nowadays: two days of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: Because there are two days of ראש השנה, day one follows the יש אומרים, and day two reads the עקידה with the הפטרה of הבן יקיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nowadays, since there are two days, on the first day we follow the 'some say' opinion. On the next day we read 'And God tested אברהם,' and the הפטרה is 'Is אפרים My dear son?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how we actually practice today, now that ראש השנה has two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the עצרת ruling in Step 12: the second day lets us use material from more than one opinion. The first day follows the יש אומרים reading about שרה. The Torah reading for the second day is the עקידה, a new choice that recalls אברהם's merit on the day of judgment. The second day keeps the first opinion's הפטרה, הבן יקיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays
Two days (of the holiday)
The first day
On the next day
Tested: the עקידה (binding of יצחק)

steps.confusionAlert: The second day does not simply read the first opinion's Torah portion (בחדש השביעי). It reads the עקידה, and only the הפטרה comes from the first opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: Our practice: ראש השנה day one is שרה and חנה. Day two is the עקידה with הבן יקיר.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when there are two days,
the first day follows the 'some say' opinion,
on the next day: 'And God tested Abraham,'
and for the haftara: 'Is [Ephraim My] dear son?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two ראש השנה opinions to today's two-day practice, the same way step 12 did for עצרת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Day one: וה׳ פקד את שרה with חנה. Day two: the עקידה with הבן יקיר.

steps.title: The readings for יום הכפורים, morning and afternoon
steps.stepSummary: On יום הכפורים the morning reading is אחרי מות with the הפטרה of כי כה אמר רם ונשא. At מנחה the reading is עריות with the הפטרה of ספר יונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום הכפורים we read 'After the death' and the הפטרה 'For thus says the High and Lofty One.' At מנחה we read the section of forbidden relationships, and the הפטרה is the book of יונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the readings for יום הכפורים, both in the morning and at מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning Torah reading describes the כהן גדול's יום כפור service. Its הפטרה (ישעיהו 57-58) talks about real fasting and תשובה. At מנחה, the section of עריות warns people about these serious sins so they will do תשובה. ספר יונה shows how the people of נינוה repented.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement
'After the death' (ויקרא 16), the יום כפור service
High and Lofty, a description of God in the הפטרה
The afternoon prayer
Forbidden relationships (ויקרא 18)

phrases.english: On Yom Kippur they read 'After the death,'
and for the haftara: 'For thus says the High and Lofty One.'
And at Mincha they read the section of forbidden relations,
and for the haftara they read Jonah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side comment about today's practice, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's list and moves on to יום הכפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Morning: אחרי מות with רם ונשא. מנחה: עריות with יונה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: God's might always comes with His humility
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that wherever the Torah describes God's גבורה, it also describes His ענוה, and that this appears in תורה, נביאים, and כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, Blessed be He, you also find His humility. This is written in the תורה, repeated in the נביאים, and said a third time in the כתובים.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the יום כפור הפטרה calls God 'רם ונשא' and then says He dwells with the lowly, the גמרא brings a related teaching by רבי יוחנן. The last line announces three proofs, which the גמרא will give in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side teaching (אגדה) set off by the wording of the הפטרה just mentioned. רבי יוחנן's claim is that God's power and His closeness to the humble always appear side by side in a פסוק. He says this shows up in all three parts of תנ״ך, and the actual verses come right after.

keyTerms.meaning: His might or greatness
His humility
Repeated (said a second time)
Said a third time
The Writings, the third part of תנ״ך

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the יום כפור הפטרה was chosen: on the day God sits in judgment in His greatness, He is also close to the broken-hearted who do תשובה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Every place that you find
the might of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
you find His humility.
This matter is written in the Torah,
repeated in the Prophets, and stated a third time in the Writings.
phrases.notes: Sets up the three proofs that follow

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גְּבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching set off by the phrase 'רם ונשא' in the יום כפור הפטרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's גבורה and ענוה always appear together in פסוקים, in all three parts of תנ״ך.

steps.title: Proof from the Torah: God of gods, who cares for orphans and widows
steps.stepSummary: The first proof for רבי יוחנן's rule comes from the תורה. God is called 'God of gods,' and the very next verse says He does justice for the orphan and the widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written in the Torah: 'For ה׳ your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords,' and right after it is written: 'He does justice for the orphan and the widow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first of three proofs for רבי יוחנן's rule. This one comes from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse describes God's power: He is above every other power. The next verse shows His humility: this same great God personally cares for the weakest people. The two ideas sit side by side, exactly as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: God's greatness and power
God's humility, His caring for the lowly
after it, right next to it
orphan and widow, the weakest members of society

phrases.english: It is written in the Torah:
'For ה׳ your God is
the God of gods and the Lord of lords,'
and it is written right after it:
'He does justice for the orphan and the widow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the תורה example for רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that God's greatness and humility appear together

steps.title: Proof from the Prophets: the High and Lofty One is with the humble
steps.stepSummary: The second proof comes from נביאים. ישעיהו calls God 'High and Lofty,' and then says God dwells with the crushed and lowly in spirit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is repeated in the Prophets: 'So says the High and Lofty One, who lives forever, and whose name is holy,' and right after it is written: 'and with the crushed and lowly in spirit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second proof, this time from נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same verse that opens the יום הכפורים הפטרה from Step 15. That is probably why רבי יוחנן's teaching was brought here. God is described as high and holy, and then He chooses to be with broken, humble people.

keyTerms.meaning: repeated (a second time) in the Prophets
High and Lofty, a name showing God's greatness
crushed and lowly in spirit

phrases.english: It is repeated in the Prophets:
'So says the High and Lofty One,
who lives forever, and is holy, etc.,'
and it is written right after it:
'and with the crushed and lowly in spirit,'
phrases.notes: God dwells with them. This is His humility.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second example of the same pattern, now from נביאים.

steps.title: Proof from the Writings: He rides the heavens and is a father to orphans
steps.stepSummary: The third proof comes from כתובים. תהילים praises God who rides the heavens, and then calls Him the father of orphans and judge of widows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is stated a third time in the Writings, as it is written: 'Praise Him who rides the heavens, whose name is Kah,' and right after it is written: 'Father of orphans and judge of widows.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the third and final proof, from כתובים. This completes רבי יוחנן's claim that the pattern appears in all three parts of תנ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God rides above the highest heavens, which is greatness. Yet He acts like a father to orphans and defends widows, which is humility. With this, all three sections of תנ״ך have shown the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: stated a third time, in the Writings
He who rides the high heavens
father of orphans
judge (defender) of widows

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's lesson: every time תנ״ך shows God's greatness, it also shows His humility. There is one example each from תורה, נביאים, and כתובים.

phrases.english: It is stated a third time in the Writings, as it is written:
'Praise Him who rides the high heavens,
whose name is Kah,'
and it is written right after it:
'Father of orphans and judge of widows.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part proof and closes the aggadic side point.

steps.title: Reading for the first day of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא returns to its list of readings. On the first day of סוכות we read the holiday section in ויקרא, and the הפטרה is 'Behold, a day is coming for ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first holiday day of סוכות, they read the section of the holidays in תורת כהנים (ויקרא), and the הפטרה is 'Behold, a day is coming for ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the side point about God's humility, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's list of holiday readings. It now reaches סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah reading is ויקרא chapter 23, which lists all the holidays, including סוכות. The הפטרה is זכריה chapter 14, which speaks about all nations coming to celebrate סוכות in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Festival,' the usual name for סוכות in the ברייתא
the section listing the holidays (ויקרא 23)
the book of ויקרא
they read as the הפטרה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חַג' with no other word means סוכות specifically. It does not mean any holiday.

phrases.english: On the first holiday day of the Festival (Sukkos)
they read the section of the holidays
that is in Leviticus,
and the haftara is 'Behold, a day is coming for ה׳.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list of readings after the aggadic side point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first day of סוכות: ויקרא 23 with the הפטרה of זכריה 14.

steps.title: The second day of סוכות nowadays
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays there are two holiday days. On the second day we read the same Torah portion, and the הפטרה is 'And they gathered to King שלמה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when there are two days, on the next day we read the same Torah portion. What is the הפטרה? 'And they gathered to King שלמה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note for today's second holiday day outside ארץ ישראל. It asks what to read and answers in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah reading stays the same as on the first day. Only the הפטרה changes. The new הפטרה (מלכים א chapter 8) describes the people gathering to שלמה at the בית המקדש dedication, which happened on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: nowadays
two days (the extra day kept outside ארץ ישראל)
for the הפטרה

phrases.english: And nowadays, when there are two days,
on the next day we read the same Torah portion too,
what do we read as the haftara?
phrases.notes: A simple question that is answered right away.

phrases.english: 'And they gathered to King Solomon.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies Step 20 to the second day kept today, and adds a different הפטרה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Second day of סוכות: the same Torah reading, with the הפטרה of 'ויקהלו אל המלך שלמה.'

steps.title: חול המועד readings and the last day of the Festival
steps.stepSummary: On the other days of סוכות we read about the holiday קרבנות. On the last holiday day (שמיני עצרת) we read 'כל הבכור,' and the הפטרה is 'ויהי ככלות שלמה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And on all the other days of the Festival, they read about the Festival's offerings. On the last holiday day, they read 'All the firstborn,' which contains מצוות, statutes, and the firstborn, and the הפטרה is 'And it was when שלמה finished.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list. It covers the middle days of סוכות and then the final holiday day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle days use במדבר chapter 29, which lists each day's קרבנות. The last day uses the section in דברים that starts with tithes and charity laws and ends with firstborn animals and the holidays. The הפטרה tells what שלמה did when he finished praying at the dedication, an event that took place on this day.

keyTerms.meaning: the offerings of סוכות (במדבר 29)
the last holiday day, i.e. שמיני עצרת
'All the firstborn,' the name of the reading in דברים 15
מצוות and statutes; the reading starts earlier, with laws of tithes and gifts to the poor

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the reading is called 'כל הבכור,' it actually starts earlier, at 'עשר תעשר.' The words 'מצות וחוקים ובכור' tell you the reading covers those earlier laws and ends with the firstborn.

phrases.english: And on all the other days of the Festival
they read about the offerings of the Festival.
On the last holiday day they read 'All the firstborn,'
which has מצוות, statutes, and the firstborn,
and the haftara is 'And it was when Solomon finished.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list past the first day of סוכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Middle days: the קרבנות of סוכות. שמיני עצרת: 'כל הבכור' with the הפטרה of 'ויהי ככלות שלמה.'

steps.title: The next day: reading וזאת הברכה
steps.stepSummary: On the day after שמיני עצרת (the second day kept outside ארץ ישראל) we read 'וזאת הברכה,' and the הפטרה is 'ויעמד שלמה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On the next day they read 'And this is the blessing,' and the הפטרה is 'And שלמה stood.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line gives the readings for the extra day after שמיני עצרת. That is the day we now call שמחת תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this day the Torah reading reaches the very end of the תורה, the last section of דברים. The הפטרה is the middle part of the same story in מלכים א chapter 8, where שלמה stands and prays at the dedication of the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: the next day (the second day of שמיני עצרת)
the last פרשה of the תורה
'And שלמה stood' (מלכים א 8:22), שלמה's prayer

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for finishing the תורה on the second day of שמיני עצרת. That day is what we know as שמחת תורה.

phrases.english: On the next day they read 'And this is the blessing,'
and the haftara is 'And Solomon stood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second day of שמיני עצרת right after the readings for the last holiday day.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Second day of שמיני עצרת: 'וזאת הברכה' with the הפטרה of 'ויעמד שלמה.'

steps.title: שבת during חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב: on a שבת during חול המועד, of either פסח or סוכות, we read 'ראה אתה.' The הפטרה is the dry bones on פסח and the war of גוג on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: When שבת falls on חול המועד, whether on פסח or on סוכות, we read 'See, You.' For the הפטרה: on פסח, 'The dry bones,' and on סוכות, 'On the day גוג comes.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a new rule for a special case: a שבת that falls in the middle days of a holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah reading is the same for both holidays: שמות 33-34, which includes the laws of the holidays. Only the הפטרה changes. On פסח we read about the dry bones coming back to life, which is a picture of redemption. On סוכות we read about the war of גוג, which is about the final redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: the middle days of the holiday (חול המועד)
'See, You,' the reading in שמות 33:12
the dry bones (יחזקאל 37)
the enemy king in the war of the end of days (יחזקאל 38)

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת חול המועד the Torah reading is always 'ראה אתה.' The הפטרה is the dry bones on פסח and גוג on סוכות.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: When Shabbos falls on the intermediate days of the holiday,
whether on Pesach or on Sukkos,
for the Torah reading we read 'See, You.'
For the haftara, on Pesach: 'The dry bones.'
And on Sukkos: 'On the day Gog comes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא's day-by-day list to deal with the special case of שבת during חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת חול המועד: 'ראה אתה,' with the הפטרה of the dry bones on פסח and 'ביום בא גוג' on סוכות.

steps.title: חנוכה reading: the נשיאים, with the lamps of זכריה
steps.stepSummary: On חנוכה we read about the gifts of the נשיאים, and the הפטרה is the lamps of זכריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On חנוכה we read the section of the princes. The הפטרה is the section of the lamps in זכריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of readings and moves on to חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah reading is about the נשיאים bringing gifts when the משכן's מזבח was dedicated. That fits חנוכה, which also celebrates a dedication. The הפטרה from זכריה describes a golden מנורה, which matches the lights of חנוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The eight-day holiday celebrating the rededication of the בית המקדש
The tribal princes who brought dedication gifts for the מזבח (במדבר ז)
The vision of the golden מנורה in the book of זכריה
They read as the הפטרה

phrases.english: On Chanukah — we read the section of the princes,
phrases.notes: במדבר פרק ז, the dedication of the מזבח

phrases.english: and for the haftarah we read the lamps of Zechariah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's list after רב הונא's statement about שבת חול המועד. The ברייתא's own list moves from the סוכות readings to חנוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חנוכה we read the נשיאים, and the הפטרה is the lamps of זכריה.

steps.title: Two שבתות of חנוכה: זכריה first, then שלמה
steps.stepSummary: If חנוכה has two שבתות, the first uses the lamps of זכריה and the second uses the lamps of שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there happen to be two שבתות during חנוכה, on the first we read the lamps of זכריה as the הפטרה. On the second we read the lamps of שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical detail to the ברייתא. It explains what to do when חנוכה has two שבתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave only one הפטרה for חנוכה. Since חנוכה lasts eight days, it can include two שבתות. The second שבת needs its own הפטרה, so the גמרא assigns the lamps that שלמה made for the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: It happens, it occurs
The first one
The last one, the second one
The lamps that שלמה made for the בית המקדש (מלכים א ז)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not part of the ברייתא's list. It is the גמרא's own addition, just like the 'nowadays' additions in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: And if it happens that there are two Shabbatot (during Chanukah) —
on the first, we read the lamps of Zechariah,
on the second, we read the lamps of Solomon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical extension to the חנוכה הפטרה given in step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: First שבת חנוכה: lamps of זכריה. Second שבת חנוכה: lamps of שלמה.

steps.title: פורים reading: 'ויבא עמלק'
steps.stepSummary: On פורים we read the section of the war with עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: On פורים we read 'And עמלק came.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to פורים and gives its Torah reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן came from עמלק. So on פורים we read about the first time עמלק attacked the Jewish people (שמות יז). The reading ties the story of the מגילה back to the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiday celebrating the rescue from המן
'And עמלק came', the Torah section in שמות יז:ח–טז

phrases.english: On Purim — we read "And Amalek came."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the ברייתא's list after חנוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פורים the Torah reading is 'ויבא עמלק'.

steps.title: New Moon reading: 'And in the beginnings of your months'
steps.stepSummary: On ראש חודש we read the section about the קרבנות of ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש חודש we read 'And on the beginnings of your months.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the Torah reading for ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section in במדבר כח lists the extra קרבנות (מוסף) brought on ראש חודש. Like the holidays, the reading fits the day's own קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of the new month (plural of ראש חודש)
'And on the beginnings of your months', the section in במדבר כח:יא–טו

phrases.english: On the New Moons — we read "And on the beginnings of your months."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the ברייתא's list after פורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש חודש the Torah reading is 'ובראשי חדשיכם'.

steps.title: Special הפטרות when ראש חודש falls on שבת or on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: When ראש חודש is on שבת, the הפטרה is 'והיה מדי חדש בחדשו'. When ראש חודש is on Sunday, the שבת before has the הפטרה 'מחר חדש'. This passage then opens a new statement by רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ראש חודש falls on שבת, the הפטרה is 'And it shall be, every new month.' When it falls on Sunday, on the day before (שבת) the הפטרה is 'And יהונתן said to him: Tomorrow is the new month.' רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives special הפטרות for when ראש חודש lands on שבת or on Sunday. At the very end, the גמרא begins a new statement from רב הונא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ישעיה סו mentions both ראש חודש and שבת, so it fits a שבת that is also ראש חודש. When ראש חודש is on Sunday, the שבת is its eve. So we read the story of דוד and יהונתן, which took place on the day before ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: It falls out on (a certain day)
The first day of the week, Sunday
On the day before
'Tomorrow is the new month' (שמואל א כ)

steps.whatToRemember: Each special day has a matching reading. ראש חודש on שבת uses 'השמים כסאי' (which ends with 'והיה מדי חדש'). ראש חודש on Sunday means the שבת before uses 'מחר חדש'.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'מחר חדש' הפטרה is read on שבת, not on ראש חודש itself. It is read on the day before, because that is the day the story describes.

phrases.english: When the New Moon falls on Shabbat,
for the haftarah we read "And it shall be, every new month."
phrases.notes: ישעיה סו, a verse that mentions both ראש חודש and שבת

phrases.english: If it falls on Sunday,
on the day before (Shabbat) we read as the haftarah
"And Jonathan said to him: Tomorrow is the New Moon."
Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: This starts something new from רב הונא, but his actual words carry on over on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds special הפטרה rules to the ראש חודש reading in step 28. It ends by opening רב הונא's next statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראש חודש on שבת: the הפטרה is 'והיה מדי חדש בחדשו'. ראש חודש on Sunday: the preceding שבת's הפטרה is 'מחר חדש'.
